closure_evidence.technical: Reproduced the item's own reported false-retirement class locally: with the (a) test-scale fix applied (S=20ms, RetryBudget 80ms, exactly as left in the uncommitted working tree), TestDeadRailResetsRetryBudget alone failed 11/20 (55%) with no artificial load beyond this host's ambient 3.4-4.0 load average -- worse than m5-hermes's own 10/50 (20%) at S=5ms under a deliberate load=9.0 CPU-spinner rig. Also ran the full TestDeadRail* suite at the unmodified, currently-committed thresholds and found 8 of ~10 tests failing the same way, confirming this specific host cannot currently give a clean pass/fail signal for this suite's wall-clock-timing assumptions at all (consistent with the standing reference_m5_fabric_oversubscription_permanent finding that this fabric host is permanently oversubscribed). Concluded option (a) is not a fix, only margin, and reverted the uncommitted attempt. Chose option (b) -- dark persistence (require the peer's dark mark on two consecutive NACK masks before a silence conviction, in the retire loop at reliable.go:3521) -- as the correctness fix, since fakeRail's lack of FIONREAD reader-behind immunity is a real gap m5-hermes already identified that could extend to any future non-fd rail. Did not build (b) myself: checkDeadRailSilence is an 8+-round metal-tuned state machine (H5.1 -> H5.1b -> H5.2 rounds 2-8) and a conviction-rule change needs the same three-arm metal rerun m5-hermes's harness already produces -- not reproducible or safely hand-built from this seat blind to that tuning history.
closure_evidence.operational: No merge action was required or taken on PR #278 -- it was already MERGED before this item arrived in the claude-io inbox (evidence-only PR, no code changes). This closure adds the (a)-vs-(b) decision the item explicitly left open, as a new evidence commit (PR pending review), and routes the actual (b) implementation + metal verification back to m5-hermes rather than claiming it done.

Rather than pick blind, spent the review cycle actually running the cheaper option (a) first to see whether it closed the gap -- it measurably did not, on this specific shared host, which is itself useful signal (this host is not a reliable place to validate this suite's tunings at all while the agent fabric is live on it, per standing canon). The harder, correct fix (b) is handed back to the metal-rig owner rather than half-built here without the three-arm verification discipline every prior round of this state machine has required.
